properties.name: reflow2 keeps working entirely on one machine — no network, no sign-in, no server elsewhere — for anyone who wants it that way
properties.statement:
A person shall always be able to run reflow2 completely locally, as it runs today: the design store on their own disk, the agent talking to it over stdio or through `--shared` on loopback, with no network, no account, no sign-in and no server anywhere else. Remote servers (flo2's api.flo2.io, an organization's shared server) are options added beside this, never a replacement for it, and never a precondition of it.

IN ANTHONY'S WORDS, 2026-09-25: "we're not getting rid of the current local only setup for reflow2 (basically how I'm using it now)? I still want the option to use it completely locally."

CONSISTENT WITH WHAT IS ALREADY RECORDED: dec:idea-authentication-is-somebody-elses-layer-and-the-line-is-the-contributor-id draws the line that stdio and loopback `--shared` never meet an authentication step, and Anthony said on 2026-08-26: "I don't do any authentication and I don't want to change that by adding in some authentication step."
